meaning: The quasi-realist regroup on the robust-truth deviation target (#190), after Dreier as SEP §5.2 reports him. From the same minimalist premises as the collapse argument, every moral sentence is minimally truth-apt. None is robustly truth-apt: robust moral truth would actually explain our thought and talk (the explanatory bridge STMT-ROBUST-MORAL-TRUTH-IS-EXPLANATORY, an unattributed open premise: Dreier as reported says only that robust truth is suited to explanatory work, STMT-ROBUST-MORAL-TRUTH-SUITED-TO-EXPLAIN, and suitedToExplainDoesNotGiveBridge shows that this does not supply the bridge), but on the anti-realist order our thought and talk explain moral truth instead, and the two orders exclude each other (the unattributed open premise STMT-EXPLANATORY-ORDER-ASYMMETRIC). So quasi-realism's answer to Q-ROBUST-TRUTH follows: the minimal/robust contrast is sustained. The corollary antirealistOrderExcludesCollapse composes with MINIMALISM-COLLAPSES-ROBUST-TRUTH-DEVIATION: with a moral sentence, these premises are inconsistent with the collapse premise. quasiRealistDataDoNotRequireRobustTruth is a model in which the minimalist premises, a moral sentence and quasi-realism's answer hold and realism's robust answer fails, so the data the quasi-realist accepts do not by themselves require the robust answer. Countermodels show each of the five premises is needed. Scope: the anti-realist order, the explanatory bridge and the asymmetry are open; the deviation therefore stays open and turns on the order of explanation (Q-EXPLANATORY-ORDER, and through it Q-MORAL-GROUNDING, #191). There is no refutes relation in either direction.
